catalog_quote: El sistema de acentuación del 'weenhayek no se deja resumir en ninguna regla simple y general para todas las categorías de palabras. En términos fonológicos, sin miramientos a la morfología, se puede describir el acento prosódico del idioma como libre. [...] Las variaciones de acentuación también producen pares mínimos: (45) yikphà' 'se va río arriba' yíkphà' 'se va hacia arriba (en el aire)' [...] 'íihikye' 'existen' 'iihíkye' 'existiría (-hí- = IRREALIS) [...] Obsérvese, además, que el acento primario de la palabra no depende de la duración o del peso de la sílaba. El acento primario es insensible a la cantidad de las sílabas. [...] La regla general para la acentuación de los sustantivos es que tienen acento primario final. [...] Por causa de la variabilidad de la ubicación del acento primario de la palabra no es posible establecer reglas de acentuación que tengun validez general para todo el vocabulario del idioma. [...] Una palabra 'weenhayek puede tener un máximo de dos sílabas prominentes; si son dos, la que tiene vocal larga, recibe acento secundario. [...] Por una parte hay un principio que asigna el acento primario de la palabra a la última sílaba. Este mecanismo opera indistintamente, prescindiendo del peso y de la estructura interior de la sílaba. [...] Sin embargo, es evidente que no es generalmente predecible la acentuación del 'weenhayek. La homogeneidad que caracteriza los sustantivos no tiene validez general para otras categorías de palabras.

new_statements.translation: The accentuation system of 'Weenhayek cannot be summed up in any simple, general rule valid for all word classes. In phonological terms, without regard to morphology, the prosodic accent of the language can be described as free. [...] The general rule for the accentuation of nouns is that they have final primary stress. [...] there is a principle that assigns the primary stress of the word to the last syllable. This mechanism operates indiscriminately, regardless of the weight and internal structure of the syllable. [...] However, it is evident that 'Weenhayek accentuation is not generally predictable. The homogeneity that characterises nouns does not hold generally for other word classes.

En terminos fonologicos, sin miramientos a la morfologia, se puede describir el acento prosodico…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Default/majority pattern is word-final primary stress: nouns of all classes and lengths (including compounds and suffixed nouns) are oxytone, assigned to the last syllable irrespective of syllable weight, and the author's 2017 grammar adds that 'la gran mayoría de las palabras son agudas' so only non-oxytone words are marked orthographically. But the author himself characterises the accent as phonologically free/contrastive: quality words and especially verbs may be paroxytone or proparoxytone, verbal suffixes differ in whether they attract stress (with several suffixes stress falls on one of the last two syllables), and there are stress minimal pairs. Nikulin & Carol 2024 re-read the same data as rightmost-syllable stress with lexically extrametrical verbal suffixes ('mostly predictable'). Coded fixed: final syllable (default) with morphological/lexical exceptions; an alternative strict coding from the author's own label would be lexical/free.
new_statements.secondary_stress: A word has at most one long vowel and at most two prominent syllables; when primary (final) stress is elsewhere, the syllable containing the long vowel receives secondary stress (e.g. noowatshankyeyaj 'vida': primary on last, secondary on first). Only VV counts as heavy (VC does not); Claesson analyses nouns as unbounded, right-headed, quantity-sensitive feet (sec. 11 pp. 19-21). Primary stress itself is quantity-insensitive.
new_statements.exceptions: Nouns with non-final stress: ijwáala 'día, sol', móoso 'mozo' (Spanish loan), ajwúumaq 'cadáver' (fn. 16 p. 19). Quality words: mostly final (pitaaj, jwitsaaj) but also omáatkye, wáasi, qáatsiya, qóoqayeh (p. 18). Verbs: yahóoyeh vs yahoope, yahúuteh vs yahuutwek; stress stays on the radical in ohúuteh, yahóoyejeh, latíihi but is final in opààyneh, oyààpnho (pp. 22-23). Minimal pairs: yikphà 'se va río arriba' / yíkphà 'se va hacia arriba (en el aire)', tàlhphà / tâlhphà, íihikye 'existen' / iihíkye 'existiría', lheekye 'su pierna' / lhéekye 'existes', latààlhe 'retoño' / latâàlheh 'vienes de' (pp. 18-19).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (isolated inflected word forms, effectively citation/pre-pausal forms: Claesson notes final laryngeals ʔ/h surface only before pause). Orthographic convention: accent written only on non-oxytone words. Avram 2008 (Misión La Paz, Argentine Pilcomayo; filed under wich1262 by Glottolog) independently reports 'ultimate stress' in single words (sec. 4.5 pp. 79-80) while older pan-Wichí sources (Hunt, Tovar) describe sentence-rhythm-driven accent.
new_statements.identity_note: Claesson's description is of 'Weenhayek proper (formerly 'Mataco-Noctén/Noctenes'), recorded mainly at Villa Montes, Tarija, Bolivia (upper Pilcomayo) in the 1980s-90s = Glottolog wich1262 'Weenhayek', iso mtp. Avram 2008 describes Wichí of Misión La Paz, Salta, Argentina (lower Pilcomayo, Argentine bank); Glottolog 5.1 files the La Paz variety under wich1262 (it lists Fernández Garay 2007 'Paraje La Paz' there), although Argentine Pilcomayo Wichí is elsewhere labelled Güisnay (wich1264). Nercesian 2011 (Bermejo dialect, Formosa) and Terraza 2009 (Rivadavia, Salta) describe other varieties (wich1263/wich1264 area) and are used here only for their second-hand report of Claesson 1994. The house catalog already has wich1263 (Vejoz; Tovar 1981, PHRASAL); this entry is distinct.

He notes that the suffixation of transitivizers or other role markers results in "paroxytone and proparoxytone words"'; her own analysis (Bermejo dialect, Formosa) puts primary stress on the rightmost iambic foot.
